title_or_context: West Rand property authority service area
observation: The agency uses West Rand for a service area including Roodepoort, Randburg, Krugersdorp, Randfontein and associated suburbs.
limitations: Promotional service area; broad scope is evidence of usage, not consensus membership.

title_or_context: West Rand property alias and trends
observation: The West Rand alias is used for Krugersdorp, Randfontein and Westonaria, with a materially different scope from the broader Private Property grouping.
limitations: The disagreement is retained; no portal alias is adopted wholesale.

title_or_context: Pretoria Old East estate agency market
observation: Old East is used as a current premium market around Hazelwood, Lynnwood, Erasmusrand, Monument Park and related eastern suburbs.
limitations: Premium agency coverage may underrepresent affordable parts of the broader East.

publisher: The Citizen / Pam Golding network content
title_or_context: Johannesburg South and Alberton property market
observation: Johannesburg South is described as a broad value-oriented market including Alberton and southern Johannesburg suburbs such as Mulbarton, Linmeyer, Oakdene, Mondeor and Winchester Hills.
limitations: Republished agency material; publication context and current inventory are not a boundary authority.

title_or_context: Johannesburg West property search market page
observation: The agency exposes Johannesburg West as a consumer property-search concept, separate from a single suburb page.
limitations: Search landing pages are editorial/product groupings and may change with inventory.

observation: Faerie Glen is explicitly described as one of the most popular Pretoria East suburbs and connected to Old and New East.
limitations: Single-suburb agency page; supports a core member, not the full market.

observation: The official spatial document treats the Vaal urban core as a cross-boundary system including Meyerton, Vereeniging, Sebokeng/Evaton, Vanderbijlpark and Sasolburg.
limitations: Spatial-planning geography is not a property-search taxonomy; it establishes the cross-province scope issue only.

title_or_context: Johannesburg East narrow market basket reported from Lightstone
observation: The publication reports a narrow Johannesburg East basket around Highlands North and nearby inner-eastern suburbs, contrasting with wider East Rand usage.
limitations: The article reports third-party analysis and is historical; it is retained as conflict evidence, not as a boundary authority.

publisher: Property24 / Seeff and RE/MAX market commentary
observation: Current commentary names Woodhill, Mooikloof, Silver Lakes, The Hills and Six Fountains and relates Pretoria East to eastern suburbs and schools.
limitations: A publication article summarises agency views; use for consensus themes, not exact edges.

title_or_context: Johannesburg East / East Rand housing market
observation: The article uses Johannesburg East for a broad basket reaching Kempton Park, Bedfordview, Benoni, Boksburg, Brakpan, Linksfield and Edenvale.
limitations: Older editorial usage and possible conflation with East Rand make this evidence for ambiguity, not a launch definition.

observation: The Vaal Triangle is used as a meaningful residential market around Vereeniging, Vanderbijlpark and Meyerton, with buyer and affordability commentary.
limitations: The market term can cross into Sasolburg and Free State; Gauteng scope must be governed separately.

observation: Centurion is presented as a substantial market between Johannesburg and Pretoria with roughly 40 suburbs and many estates.
limitations: Agency count is directional and not used as a precise boundary.

observation: Moot is used as a local Pretoria property-market label by a dedicated agency.
limitations: Single-agency coverage; the wider Moot list is cross-checked against Chas Everitt's Pretoria profile.

observation: Pretoria West has a direct neighbourhood page and property inventory.
limitations: No sufficiently independent, stable broader membership set was established.

observation: Pretoria North is treated both as a suburb and as an area-market reference for northern Pretoria and Rosslyn-related property.
limitations: The same-name collision requires type-aware disambiguation.

observation: The agency markets Johannesburg East coverage across Benoni, Boksburg, Kempton Park, Springs, Brakpan, Germiston and Edenvale.
limitations: A service-area statement is not independent proof of a stable consumer boundary.

observation: Pretoria North East is used for a broad set including Annlin, Doornpoort, East Lynne, Gezina, Magalieskruin, Montana, Mamelodi and related nodes.
limitations: The portal grouping is broad and not sufficiently corroborated for launch.

title_or_context: East Rand property alias and trends
observation: The East Rand alias is high-volume and includes Boksburg, Brakpan, Kempton Park, Tembisa, Benoni, Germiston and Springs.
limitations: The alias list is a discovery aid and differs from Private Property's wider list.

observation: A second agency uses Pretoria Far East as a market-area term, confirming usage but not enough membership consensus.
limitations: No reliable bounded core was established in this cycle.

title_or_context: Midrand area profile and neighbouring markets
observation: Midrand is positioned between Centurion and Sandton, with Kyalami, Carlswald, Beulah, Vorna Valley and Noordwyk as market references.
limitations: Agency profile; it is strong market evidence but not authority to collapse related factual places.

observation: Midrand is presented as a consumer property area with listings across established suburbs, estates and development nodes.
limitations: Listing geography is a market signal, not a factual identity decision.

title_or_context: Pretoria East property buyer market overview
observation: A contemporary property-market publication describes Faerie Glen, Garsfontein, Moreleta Park, Woodhill and the outer N4 corridor as part of the Pretoria East buyer conversation.
limitations: Publication evidence is secondary and should reinforce, not establish, membership by itself.

observation: An agency markets Old East around Brooklyn, Groenkloof, Lynnwood Proper, Menlo Park, Waterkloof, Hazelwood and adjacent established suburbs.
limitations: Agency service area; overlap and naming are retained as observed evidence.

observation: The official district context describes Randfontein, Krugersdorp/Mogale City and Rand West City municipalities and does not make the property-market label equivalent to all Johannesburg West suburbs.
limitations: Administrative geography answers a different question and is used only to expose boundary conflict.

observation: Bedfordview is explicitly positioned on Johannesburg's East Rand and connected to the northern suburbs, East Rand and OR Tambo.
limitations: Local area profile, used as supporting evidence for an overlap node.

title_or_context: Johannesburg home buyers seeking value flock to the south
observation: A current agency market article treats Johannesburg South as a value-oriented market including Alberton and southern Johannesburg suburbs.
limitations: Agency editorial scope is market evidence, not a Property Listify boundary or reusable taxonomy.

observation: The buyer guide discusses Pretoria East through Waterkloof Ridge, Lynnwood, Garsfontein, Moreleta Park and Silver Lakes as recognisable buyer submarkets.
limitations: The article is a buyer guide and its selected examples are not a complete membership list.

observation: Current rental commentary connects Sandton demand with Bryanston, Fourways and Randburg, supporting overlapping northern submarkets.
limitations: Rental-market commentary is not a definition of the entire sales market.

observation: Centurion East is a recognisable consumer property submarket with estate and lifestyle development language.
limitations: Centurion East is treated as a possible narrower submarket, not the whole Centurion identity.

observation: The agency describes Johannesburg West through the Roodepoort-to-Soweto corridor, supporting recognition of the term but not a stable boundary.
limitations: Service-area copy is broad and promotional.

observation: Moreleta Park is described as taking up a substantial part of Pretoria East.
limitations: Local area profile, used as direct supporting evidence for a core member.

observation: The greater Sandton area is discussed through Sandton, Bryanston, Morningside, Rivonia, Sandown, Hyde Park, Illovo, Melrose and related northern Johannesburg suburbs.
limitations: Premium-market editorial selection is not a complete membership list.

observation: Pretoria Central is directly searchable and is better treated as a factual/urban-node query than an invented wider Search Area in this cycle.
limitations: Portal result is a direct-query observation only.

title_or_context: Johannesburg North property listings and surrounding northern suburbs
observation: A separately addressable Johannesburg North page sits in a North Riding-to-Lanseria grouping and exposes a northern-suburbs set including North Riding, Olivedale, Northgate, Sharonlea and nearby places.
limitations: Portal grouping and live inventory are proprietary and changing; the page is not adopted as a Property Listify hierarchy.

observation: The portal presents Johannesburg South as a multi-suburb discovery area including Bassonia, Glenvista, Lenasia, Oakdene, Winchester Hills and Mulbarton.
limitations: Portal neighbourhood grouping and live inventory are proprietary and changing.

observation: The Parks grouping is described around Parkhurst, Parktown North, Parkview, Parkwood, Craighall Park and Saxonwold.
limitations: Agency grouping is useful for overlap analysis, not a statutory region.

observation: Chas Everitt identifies Bassonia, Glenvista and Mulbarton as core New South property-market locations.
limitations: The article is promotional and focuses on a narrower New South concept inside the broader Johannesburg South label.

observation: A June 2026 market article reports substantial Pretoria East listing activity and treats it as a distinct property-search market.
limitations: Inventory and averages change; the demand signal does not set membership boundaries.

observation: The agency uses Johannesburg North as a large northward market concept and names Sandton, Randburg and Fourways among its coverage.
limitations: The broad wording is promotional and materially wider than an exact factual suburb.

observation: Pretoria East is a very high-volume alias with a broad list including Waterkloof, Brooklyn, Menlo Park, Moreleta Park, Faerie Glen, Equestria, Six Fountains, Silver Lakes, Woodhill and other eastern nodes.
limitations: The page is intentionally treated as noisy discovery evidence; its extended list also reaches areas normally described as North or West.

observation: Pretoria West is a directly searchable factual/property node with its own listing trends.
limitations: Current evidence supports direct factual intent more strongly than a broad supra-suburb Search Area.

observation: The city tourism source uses southern, western and northern suburb language and places Sandton, Bryanston, Randburg and Fourways in a northern context while anchoring West around Roodepoort/Krugersdorp.
limitations: Tourism geography is not property-market authority and is used only as contextual corroboration.

observation: Pretoria East is a consumer-facing area with a mix of houses, townhouses and estates and strong road access.
limitations: The profile does not provide a complete authoritative boundary.

observation: Parkview, Parktown North and Parkwood are treated as a recognisable inner-northern Johannesburg lifestyle market.
limitations: The Parks is a narrower branded market concept and should not be forced into all Johannesburg North membership.

title_or_context: Fourways and Little Fourways area profile
observation: Fourways is described as a northern Sandton suburb market with a Little Fourways cluster around Norscot, Lonehill, Beverley, Craigavon and Broadacres.
limitations: Single-agency market language; reinforces a concept but does not establish an exclusive boundary.

title_or_context: Roodepoort / Johannesburg West residential market report 2025
observation: Roodepoort is described as a Johannesburg West market spanning more than 40 suburbs.
limitations: Agency report focuses on Roodepoort and does not independently define West Rand.

observation: A high-volume Johannesburg South alias page spans Alberton, Rosettenville, Kibler Park, Mulbarton, Glenvista, Ridgeway, Bassonia, Eikenhof and surrounding southern locations.
limitations: The portal's alias scope is broad and includes places that also appear in other regional concepts.

observation: The area guide uses Pretoria East as a consumer-facing market spanning Waterkloof Glen, Lynnwood, Faerie Glen, Moreleta Park and Garsfontein, with transport corridors and lifestyle nodes as the organising context.
limitations: Local agency guide is useful market evidence but does not establish statutory boundaries.

observation: Old East is used for older suburbs including Brooklyn, Waterkloof, Menlo Park and Lynnwood.
limitations: The guide is older; it is reinforced by current agency profiles before any candidate is proposed.

observation: Gauteng South inventory includes Meyerton, Vaal Marina, Vanderbijlpark, Vereeniging, Evaton and Heidelberg, supporting a southern discovery corridor but not proving every place belongs to Vaal Triangle.
limitations: A portal region is broader than the Vaal market concept and is retained as a boundary warning.

observation: North Riding and Johannesburg North are described as northern Johannesburg suburbs connected to Fourways, Sandton, Randburg and Johannesburg CBD buyer journeys.
limitations: Editorial agency content is useful market evidence but not a neutral boundary authority.

title_or_context: Pretoria East, Old East and Moot market profiles
observation: The agency distinguishes Old Pretoria East (Waterkloof, Brooklyn, Muckleneuk, Lynnwood), New Pretoria East (Moreleta Park, Menlyn, Newlands, Garsfontein, Faerie Glen) and a Moot grouping spanning northern-central suburbs.
limitations: Agency market segmentation is strong evidence of usage but not a statutory hierarchy.

title_or_context: West Rand property market and gated developments
observation: West Rand is a high-volume property grouping with Roodepoort, Krugersdorp, Randfontein and western development nodes such as Ruimsig, Wilgeheuwel and Honeydew.
limitations: Portal region is not identical to the official district boundary.

title_or_context: Pretoria Far East farm and lifestyle market
observation: Pretoria Far East is a current consumer label for outer-east farms and lifestyle properties around Boschkop, Bashewa and Grootfontein-type locations.
limitations: The URL is a portal market alias; the observed places are not automatically factual canonical identities.

observation: A market study uses Joburg East narrowly around Highlands North, Oaklands, Orchards, The Gardens, Cheltondale, Abbotsford, Forbesdale and Hawkins Estate.
limitations: The study is dated and its narrow analytical basket conflicts with broader consumer usage.

observation: Midrand is described as stretching from Kyalami toward Centurion between Johannesburg and Pretoria, with Waterfall and other estate markets.
limitations: The guide is consumer-oriented and explicitly broad; Kyalami remains subject to its own factual evidence gate.

title_or_context: Johannesburg North property listings with nearby suburbs
observation: Johannesburg North is a distinct listing node and the page suggests a surrounding set including North Riding, Douglasdale, Noordhang, Olivedale, Northgate, Jukskei Park, Sharonlea and Sonneglans.
limitations: Surrounding-suburb suggestions are a portal discovery feature, not independent market-boundary evidence.

observation: Pretoria North is an independently addressable property node with surrounding northern suburb discovery.
limitations: The exact page proves factual/query usage, while wider market membership needs additional evidence.

observation: Fourways is presented as a Sandton/Johannesburg market comprising Fourways, Beverley, Broadacres, Craigavon, Lonehill, Magaliessig, Norscot and nearby estates.
limitations: Agency-defined area profile; estate names and boundaries are not copied as identities.

title_or_context: East Rand property market and areas
observation: East Rand is a large live property region listing Alberton, Benoni, Boksburg, Brakpan, Edenvale, Germiston, Kempton Park, Nigel, Springs, Tembisa and Katlehong.
limitations: Portal area set is evidence of consumer discovery usage, not a reusable taxonomy.

title_or_context: Midrand property market and top areas
observation: Midrand is a high-volume property node with a multi-suburb list including Noordwyk, Waterfall, Kyalami, Carlswald, Vorna Valley, Blue Hills, Halfway House and Glen Austin.
limitations: The portal list mixes factual locations, estates and developments; it is not copied.

observation: Ekurhuleni is described as Gauteng's East Rand region from Alberton through Springs and Nigel, with Boksburg, Benoni, Bedfordview, Germiston, Kempton Park, Linksfield and Modderfontein and detailed suburb examples.
limitations: The municipal label and the consumer East Rand label overlap but are not treated as identical authorities.
